title: An open benchmark and language models for AI in aging biology
description: Insilico Medicine researchers tested 18 leading AI models on LongevityBench, 17 aging-biology tasks built from real clinical, DNA-methylation, gene-expression and blood-protein data. No general model won outright, and small models trained on aging data (0.6B-9B parameters) took the top three spots. Benchmark, models and tools are open.

title: Japan approves the first iPS cell therapies: Amchepry for Parkinson's and ReHeart for heart failure
description: Japan's health ministry granted conditional, time-limited approval to Sumitomo Pharma's Amchepry (Parkinson's disease) and Cuorips' ReHeart (severe heart failure), the world's first approved products made from induced pluripotent stem cells. Both use donor cells; the first commercial transplant took place at Kyoto University Hospital in October 2026.

title: Rejuvenation of Senescent Cells, In Vitro and In Vivo, by Low-Frequency Ultrasound
description: University of Texas researchers report that low-frequency ultrasound (about 32 kHz, delivered through water) made senescent cells resume dividing without killing them, and improved physical performance in old mice. A small human trial in adults 70 and older is under way at UT Health San Antonio.
